jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Management & Organization
jobs.institution: University of Washington: Business
jobs.description:
The School of Business at the University of Washington Bothell invites applications for a Tenure-Track Assistant Professor position in Management and Organization, effective September 16, 2027. We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment to excellence in research, teaching, and service in a diverse and inclusive academic community. This is a full-time (100% FTE) position with a 9-month academic year, 3-year renewable appointment.
The successful candidate will be expected to maintain an active research program and Scholarly Academic status as defined by AACSB; publish in leading academic journals; teach a variety of undergraduate and graduate courses in management, leadership, strategy, entrepreneurship, human resources, and/or organization, based on their discipline, and provide service to the School, the University, and the community.
Applicants from all research areas of management, including but not limited to Organizational Behavior, Organization Theory, Strategic Management, Technology and Innovation Management, and Human Resource Management, are encouraged to apply.
The School of Business
The UW Bothell School of Business is accredited by AACSB and is deeply committed to the success of its faculty in research, teaching, and service. We are well known for our undergraduate, MBA, and MS Accounting programs, and enrollment has been growing at a fast pace. Located 15 miles northeast of downtown Seattle, we work closely with industry leaders, many of whom are headquartered in the region, as well as smaller, innovative, and rapidly growing companies in software, retail, medical equipment, biotechnology, electronics, and aerospace sectors. Our students are drawn from and work in companies such as Alaska Airlines, Amazon, Amgen, Boeing, Costco, Expedia, Google, ICOS, Meta, Microsoft, Nintendo, Nvidia, Phillips, PACCAR, REI, Starbucks, Symetra, T-Mobile, Tableau, and Zillow, as well as in local, State, and Federal government.
The School’s Management and Organization faculty (Stephen Jones, Sophie Leroy, Misha Mariam, Denis Trapido, Vivian Xiao) are active scholars whose work has been published in leading journals including the Academy of Management Journal, Academy of Management Annals, American Journal of Sociology, Administrative Science Quarterly, Journal of Applied Psychology, Journal of Management, Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, Organization Science, Personnel Psychology, Research Policy, and Strategic Management Journal. Faculty regularly serve on editorial boards of journals such as the Academy of Management Journal, Organization Science, Journal of Business and Psychology, and more.
The School of Business is an undepartmentalized School and encourages collegiality across the entire faculty. Faculty members should expect to interact with colleagues from other business disciplines. As part of UW’s tri-campus system, faculty members have complete access to the computing and library resources of the University of Washington.
University of Washington Bothell
Located in the heart of the Puget Sound region, the University of Washington Bothell is one of the most dynamic public universities in the state of Washington. UW Bothell is a student-centered campus known for engaging students through classes, team projects, and research in which students connect what they learn or create in the classroom with the broader community. This is achieved through close relationships with faculty members as teachers and mentors, and staff dedicated to student success. The academic work of the campus focuses on cross-disciplinary research, connected learning, and community engagement, and prepares students for leadership in the state of Washington and beyond.
The campus offers more than 55 undergraduate and graduate degree programs in five schools. Current UW Bothell enrollment is over 6,000 students. More than 90% of undergraduates are from Washington State, and approximately 40% are first-generation college attendees. The priorities of the University’s current Strategic Plan – “Expanding Access, Achieving Excellence”, are to enhance community and campus engagement, and advance cross-disciplinary teaching and scholarship. In addition to award winning faculty and staff, UW Bothell has been recognized for innovations in academic programming and support services designed to help students graduate on time and debt-free. It has also earned both recognition and awards for its work in the area of environmental sustainability and is just one of twelve institutions selected to join the launch cohort of the Postsecondary Data for Action Network (PDAN), a new national initiative co-led by the Institute for Higher Education Policy (IHEP) and the Association for Institutional Research (AIR). This selection places UW Bothell among a small group of colleges and universities collectively committed to using data in smarter, more student-centered ways.
Salary
The base salary range for this position will be $15,000-$17,222 per month ($135,000 to $155,000 annually), commensurate with experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department of Labor prevailing wage determination.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Management - OBSE
jobs.institution: Stony Brook University: College of Business

jobs.description:

We intend to hire at the Assistant Professor or Associate Professor level and invite applications from candidates nearing completion of their Ph.D. as well as current Assistant Professors and Associate Professors. The anticipated start date is September 1, 2027.
The position offers a competitive teaching load, competitive research support, and a salary commensurate with qualifications, rank, academic record, and experience.
We seek candidates who have demonstrated, or show high potential for, excellence in research that will have a strong impact on the field of management. We also seek candidates who have demonstrated, or show high potential for, excellence in teaching.
We are committed to fostering a welcoming and respectful academic environment by cultivating a community of scholars where all individuals feel valued. Recruiting faculty with a wide range of talents, skills, backgrounds, and experiences is a key priority. It is part of the State University of New York (SUNY) system, a center of academic excellence and an internationally recognized research institution that offers all students a world-class education. As a leading institution in STEM, health sciences, and interdisciplinary research, Stony Brook offers faculty a rich, collaborative environment.
About the College of Business
The College of Business at Stony Brook University is committed to delivering a transformative business education that prepares students for leadership roles in an evolving, technology-driven business landscape. We value interdisciplinary collaboration, an inclusive learning environment, and encourage faculty to incorporate real-world applications that emphasize ethics, innovation, and societal impact. The College offers a combination of graduate (masters of science and MBAs) and undergraduate programs to over 2500 students, making it a vibrant academic community.
Responsibilities
● Teach undergraduate and/or graduate courses in management. The position requires in-person teaching at the Stony Brook University campus
● Conduct and publish high-impact management-related research in leading peer-reviewed journals
● Provide service to the College and University through activities such as committee participation, support for accreditation efforts (e.g., AACSB), student mentorship, and engagement with community and industry
● Foster a culture of inclusion, collaboration, creativity, and mentorship to create an environment in which faculty, staff, and students from a variety of backgrounds and cultures can meet their full potential, thrive and help fulfill the role of the College of Business in SBU’s mission
General Requirements:
The College of Business and Stony Brook University are committed to creating a community where people from all backgrounds and experiences can contribute, succeed, and belong. Recruiting faculty with diverse talents, perspectives, experiences, and expertise strengthens academic excellence, enriches student learning, and advances the University’s mission.

jobs.title: Part-Time Lecturer, Social Entrepreneurship
jobs.institution: New York University: NYU Washington, DC
jobs.description:
NYU’s Washington, DC Academic Center is seeking a local, part-time lecturer to teach a three-credit undergraduate course, “Social Entrepreneurship,” every Spring semester starting Spring 2027.
The Spring semester runs from mid-January to early May. Classes meet once a week, for 2 hours and forty minutes. In addition to the time required for course preparation, classroom instruction, and assessment, the instructor is required to hold a minimum of one set 60-minute office hour per instruction day, during which the instructor will be available to meet with students.
The instructor role includes all preparation, delivery, and grading. Leveraging Washington, DC as a learning environment (e.g., a guest speakers, excursions) is an expectation for the course. Courses are to be intellectually challenging in content, and rigorous student assessment is required. We are especially interested in qualified candidates who share NYU Washington, DC’s commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and who can contribute to the diversity of intellectual life at our site.
Course Description
Social Entrepreneurship is an emerging and rapidly changing business field that examines the practice of identifying, starting and growing successful mission-driven for-profit and nonprofit ventures—that is, organizations that strive to advance social change through innovative solutions. This course, rooted in stakeholder theory, is designed to provide a socially relevant academic experience in order to help students gain in-depth insights into economic and social value creation across a number of areas including poverty alleviation, energy, health and sustainability. Students will have the opportunity to find and test new ideas and solutions to social problems, create sustainable business models, identify funding options and alternatives, learn about evolving legal and governance structures, learn how to measure social impact and scale a social enterprise to name a few. This course will provide students with a toolkit and frameworks that can be used to start a social venture, applied within a social venture or within other types of organizations to influence social change.
About NYU and NYU Washington, DC
Founded in 1831, New York University is the largest private university in the United States. The University has degree-granting campuses in New York, Abu Dhabi, and Shanghai and operates 12 global academic centers, along with research programs in more than 25 countries. NYU Washington, DC is one of NYU’s global academic centers where students can participate in study away while earning credits towards their degree. To learn more about NYU Washington, DC please visit the website: https://www.nyu.edu/washington-dc.html

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate in the Cognitive Science of Values
jobs.institution: Princeton University: Cognitive Science
jobs.description:
The Program in Cognitive Science, in collaboration with the University Center for Human Values, invites applications for a Postdoctoral Research Associate in the Cognitive Science of Values for a position expected to start in September of 2027.
The successful candidate will be based in the laboratory of Dr. Tania Lombrozo in the Department of Psychology. We aim to support a highly promising scholar with a background in cognitive science or a related discipline, such as psychology or empirically informed/experimental philosophy. The scholar's research agenda should address a topic that engages with both cognitive science and values, such as the role of moral values in decision making or the role of epistemic values in belief revision. The proposed research is expected to yield both theoretical and empirical publications. Candidates will be expected to contribute the equivalent of one course each year to the University Center and/or the Department. This contribution may be fulfilled by teaching a course on a topic related to cognitive science of values ( submject to sufficient enrollments and approval by Project Directors, the Department Chair or Chairs, and the Office of the Dean of the Faculty) or service to the Project or Center of some other sort, subject to approval of the Project and Center Directors. If teaching a semester-long course, the successful candidate would carry the additional part-time rank of Lecturer. The postdoc will be expected to participate in a year-long research seminar for visiting fellows and Center faculty, as well as a year-long seminar for the Center’s cohort of Postdoctoral Associates. (Each of these seminars meets roughly every other week.) The postdoc will also be expected to regularly attend talks, panels, and conferences sponsored by the Center.
The candidate will be appointed in the Program in Cognitive Science and will be invited to participate in programs of the University Center for Human Values.

jobs.title: The Roberto C. Goizueta Distinguished Presidential Residence Program 2027-2028
jobs.institution: University of Miami: Cuban Heritage Collection
jobs.description:
The Cuban Heritage Collection at the University of Miami Libraries invites applications for the 2027–2028 Roberto C. Goizueta Distinguished Presidential Residence program. Inaugurated in 2023 through the generous support of The Goizueta Foundation, this fellowship program welcomes senior scholars and public intellectuals from around the world to spend one semester (5 months) in residence at the Cuban Heritage Collection to take advantage of its vast repository of materials on Cuba and the global Cuban diaspora.
The fellows' main charge is to advance in-depth research and writing toward a project of broad scholarly or public significance (typically a book) that relates to a particular area of the Collection and the study of Cuba and/or the Cuban diaspora, broadly defined. As part of their residency, fellows will also deliver a public lecture open to the University and South Florida communities.
Distinguished fellows for the 2027–2028 cycle will begin their residence at the Cuban Heritage Collection no earlier than August 1, 2027, and conclude no later than May 31, 2028. The Collection will award two one-semester fellowships, during the Fall and Spring semesters respectively, following a thorough review of the applicant pool. Applications are reviewed by the Collection's faculty and members of its Academic Advisory Committee.
By providing time, resources, and space for writing and research, the program seeks to strengthen the Collection's reputation as a premier destination for interdisciplinary research in Cuban studies.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Fellows advance in-depth research and writing toward a project of broad scholarly or public significance (typically a book) based on a particular area of the Collection and related to Cuba and/or the Cuban diaspora, broadly defined.
Drawing on their research at the collection, fellows deliver a public lecture open to UM faculty, students, and the greater South Florida community toward the end of their residencies.
Fellows are expected to be in residence at the Cuban Heritage Collection during the fellowship period. This means a minimum of three full days a week conducting research in or writing from the collection. (Exceptions can be made for absences involving short-term travel, illness, and holidays.) Fellows are also highly encouraged to attend CHC public and academic events during their stay.
While this is not a teaching position, Fellows are expected to be open to engaging with University of Miami faculty, patrons of the CHC, and students in UM’s Program in Cuban Studies, whether through class visits or individual consultations. The CHC is a close partner of the undergraduate Program in Cuban Studies.

jobs.title: Junior Research Scientist in the Division of Science (Computer Science) - Sarah Nadi
jobs.institution: New York University: AD_Computer Science
jobs.description:
The SANAD lab at NYUAD is hiring a Junior Research Scientist to work with Dr. Sarah Nadi in the Division of Science (Computer Science Program) at New York University Abu Dhabi. The candidate will conduct research on programming languages and software engineering, develop open-source tools and resources, and work on publications related to their research.
The name SANAD (سند), meaning "support" in Arabic, is short for Software Analysis and Developer Support, reflecting the lab’s mission to assist developers as software systems become increasingly intricate. Ongoing research projects include detecting API misuse, analyzing program performance, measuring energy consumption, detecting security vulnerabilities, supporting library migrations, and leveraging large language models (LLMs) for software engineering and static analysis tasks. More information can be found on https://sanadlab.org.

jobs.title: Research Assistant Professor – Proposal Development & Research Advancement
jobs.institution: Vanderbilt University: Civil and Environmental Engineering
jobs.description:
The Vanderbilt Center for Sustainability, Energy, and Climate (VSEC) seeks a Research Assistant Professor to provide strategic and operational leadership in research proposal development and external funding advancement. This position will contribute both strategically and intellectually to the development of multidisciplinary research initiatives, in addition to coordinating proposal development and submission. The role will actively support VSEC’s mission by expanding the center’s capacity to identify, develop, and submit competitive proposals for externally sponsored research.
The Research Assistant Professor will work closely with the VSEC Director, VSEC Deputy Director, Director of Operations, core faculty, and affiliated researchers to cultivate and coordinate multidisciplinary teams, align faculty expertise with emerging funding opportunities, and advance short- and long-term funding strategies for the center. The position will play a vital role in strengthening VSEC’s research development infrastructure and enhancing its competitiveness for federal, foundation, industry, and other external support.

Work closely with the VSEC Director, VSEC Deputy Director, and Director of Operations to develop and implement short- and long-term funding strategies.
Manage proposal development processes from opportunity identification through final submission, including timelines, internal coordination, sponsor requirements, and submission readiness.
Develop and coordinate VSEC-centered multidisciplinary proposal teams that draw on the expertise of VSEC core faculty, affiliated investigators, research staff, postdoctoral scholars, and external collaborators as appropriate.

Maintain awareness of sponsor trends, program priorities, and evolving funding landscapes relevant to energy, sustainability, decarbonization, infrastructure, and related research areas.
Track proposal pipelines, submissions, outcomes, and resubmission opportunities to support continuous improvement in VSEC’s research development efforts.
Contribute, as appropriate, to white papers, publications, workshops, and research planning activities that help advance VSEC’s visibility and long-term research agenda.
Engage in proposal improvement processes to enhance win rates/competitiveness through narrative shaping, positioning, and team composition.
Lead and collaborate on research initiatives with VSEC faculty, researchers, and partners, contributing technical expertise to the design, execution, and advancement of research projects.
ead and contribute to the development, writing, and publication of scholarly papers, technical reports, and other research outputs.

jobs.title: Tenured/Tenure-track Position in the Department of Middle Eastern Languages and Cultures
jobs.institution: University of Pennsylvania: School of Arts and Sciences - Middle Eastern Languages and Cultures
jobs.description:
The Department of Middle Eastern Languages and Cultures at the University of Pennsylvania and the Penn Museum invite applications for a faculty-curator position in Mesopotamian Archaeology
to be appointed jointly by the Museum as a curator in the Near East Section and by the School as a tenured or tenure-track faculty member, with time, duties and responsibilities evenly split between the two roles. Faculty-curators have their teaching load reduced from four to two courses per year.
Applications are welcome from archaeologists actively engaged in fieldwork in Mesopotamia (modern Eastern Syria and Iraq) with a research focus on Mesopotamia’s historic periods. The successful candidate will carry out independent research and publication; complement current course offerings on ancient Mesopotamian cultures, history, and material remains at the undergraduate and graduate levels; supervise B.A. and M.A. theses and Ph.D. dissertations; participate in the mentorship of undergraduate and graduate students working in these areas; and engage actively in all other faculty duties.
As curator, the candidate will participate in exhibition, research, education, and outreach activities related to the collections within the Section. Experience in collections stewardship is highly desirable.
The Penn Museum
Home to over a million extraordinary artifacts and archaeological finds, the Penn Museum has been uncovering our shared humanity across continents and millennia since 1887. In bridging archaeology (the study of objects made by humans), with anthropology (the science of humanity), we chart a course for finding one’s own place in the arc of human history. We are dedicated to telling powerful stories that emerge from our own excavations and research across the world.
The curatorial appointment will be in the Museum’s Near East Section, home to over 100,000 artefacts most of which come from over a century of excavations carried out by the Museum in almost every country in the Middle East and spanning a broad range of time periods.
The Department of Middle Eastern Languages and Cultures (MELC)
MELC engages in the interdisciplinary study and teaching of the cultures and peoples of the Middle East as they have expressed themselves in languages, texts and literatures, including written and oral sources, as well as art, architecture, archaeology, and material objects. Our studies encompass the geographic region that stretches from North Africa and the Iberian Peninsula through the eastern Mediterranean to Arabia and Iran.
The areas we study primarily include Egypt, Mesopotamia, Israel/Palestine, greater Syria, Arabia, Iran and the Persianate world, and Anatolia and Turkey. We teach ancient and modern languages including Sumerian, Akkadian, Egyptian, Hebrew, Arabic, Persian, Turkish, and Kurdish. We endeavor in teaching and research to explore past and present social contacts across communities and places. In this way, we push boundaries and frontiers within and beyond the Middle East.
Our department upholds a conscious commitment to scholarship within the University of Pennsylvania and the world. The intellectual life of the Department is collaborative and flourishes from its culture of inclusion, which aspires to make everyone feel welcome. We aim to build connections to scholars across the University of Pennsylvania campus and elsewhere at local, national, and international levels as we exchange ideas and spread knowledge. This commitment to collegiality, inquiry, and exploration makes our department a vibrant center for the humanistic study of the Middle East from ancient times to the present.
The department offers an undergraduate major that provides students with an understanding of the ancient, medieval and modern Middle East. Our faculty also participate in cross-disciplinary graduate programs, such as the Art and Archaeology of the Mediterranean World.
Interdisciplinary Connections
The successful candidate will join a highly interdisciplinary collective for research and teaching, including the PhD programs in the Art and Archaeology of the Ancient World and Ancient History, as well as faculty and students in Anthropology, Art History, MELC and the Museum’s Center for the Analysis of Archaeological Materials. In addition to Penn’s groups, a strong regional collective for faculty and graduate students engages in course exchange with Bryn Mawr College, Princeton University, and Temple University.
The School of Arts and Sciences
The Department of Middle Eastern Languages and Cultures is housed within the School of Arts & Sciences, at Penn. The School is comprised of 28 academic departments, the College of Arts and Sciences, the Graduate Division, and the College of Liberal and Professional Studies. Interdisciplinary research and collaboration are supported as much by the breadth and depth of academic pursuits at Penn as well as the proximity of resources on our contiguous green urban campus in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. We promote and encourage curiosity, intellectual engagement, and discovery among all our students and faculty. University, School, and departmental resources that support our efforts/ include but are not limited to: the Offices of the Vice Provost for Faculty and Vice Provost for Research, PennGlobal, Wellness at Penn, the Center for Teaching and Learning, the Penn Center for Undergraduate Research and Fellowships, and Penn Human Resources.
Qualifications include:
● All candidates should have:
o publications appropriate to rank
o a deep commitment to teaching undergraduate and graduate students, and mentoring and supporting a diverse student body
o expertise in the archaeology of ancient Mesopotamia
o active research and fieldwork in the area of ancient Mesopotamia
o the ability to direct graduate/undergraduate research for a diverse student body
● Candidates are expected to have a PhD/postdoctoral experience/other terminal degree by the time of appointment, which is July 1, 2027.
Application instructions/Required documents:
Cover letter (2-3 pages)
CV
A research statement (3-5 pages) covering recent, present, and planned research programs
Contact information for three individuals who have agreed to provide letters of recommendation
A writing sample of no more than 40 pages will be requested from longlisted applicants
Review of applications will begin October 19th and continue until the position is filled.
Please contact Dr. Steve Tinney (stinney@sas.upenn.edu) with questions regarding the application process

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Architecture
jobs.institution: Lehigh University: Art, Architecture and Design
jobs.description:
The Department of Art, Architecture and Design at Lehigh University invites applications for a tenure-track position as Assistant Professor of Architecture, with expertise in architectural design. The anticipated start date is July 1 2027.
The successful candidate will join a large and multidisciplinary department with undergraduate BA major programs in art, architecture, graphic and product design, and art history. Through a studio culture that encourages peer engagement, collective critique, and open discourse, the department's architecture curriculum fosters engagement with the built environment in its critical, technical, and social dimensions. The standard teaching load for tenure-track faculty is two courses per semester, and the university offers exceptional support to faculty, including generous start up packages for new faculty and numerous internal grant opportunities for ongoing research and creative practice.
As a faculty member in the Department of Art, Architecture and Design, the candidate will be expected to teach introductory- through advanced-level courses in architectural design in regular rotation, as well as courses in the candidate’s areas of expertise. They will also be expected to develop and maintain an active program of scholarship and creative practice that demonstrates excellence and impact, as evidenced by built works, exhibitions, awards, reviews, publications, and other forms of juried or peer-reviewed work, or professional and client-based projects comparably recognized. In both teaching and research, the candidate’s work should be seated in methods that look to make an impact in a range of communities beyond the university setting, serving both disciplinary and public interests. In addition, they will contribute to departmental, college, and university service.
The department promotes forward-thinking scholarship and teaching, with affiliation across the university’s many interdisciplinary programs, centers, and institutes. We are a versatile and experimental program that offers exceptional research opportunities and support for faculty conducting paradigm-shifting work across the boundaries of art, architecture, and design.
About the Department of Art, Architecture and Design
The Department of Art, Architecture and Design is one of Lehigh University’s largest enrolling undergraduate departments. The department offers BA degrees in four majors—art, architecture, graphic and product design, and art history—and minors in each area, as well as in museum studies and apparel design.
We offer an undergraduate education in the arts that combines the depth of an art and design school training with the breadth and flexibility of a liberal arts curriculum. We aim to enable students to become makers and designers, builders and creators—backed by the resources of a R1-level research university that has for generations helped shape innovation, industry, and design in the United States. We also aspire to excellence and distinction in experiential learning by providing students with opportunities to harness the skills they learn in the classroom, both for real-world application and as the basis for service in the community and the world at large. We are part of the College of Arts and Sciences—the heart of Lehigh University—offering a wide variety of academic majors, minors, and interdisciplinary programs at both the undergraduate and graduate level.
The department is housed in a 40,000-square-foot research and teaching facility on Lehigh University’s Mountaintop Campus, with studio and classroom spaces serviced by extensive resources, encompassing a range of computer labs, printing and digital fabrication technologies, shops, and finishing areas. This includes adjacent resources of the university’s Design Labs, a network of fabrication facilities across campus; and the collections and exhibitions of the Lehigh University Art Galleries (LUAG), with a permanent collection of over 20,000 works of art. The department is currently expanding its community-facing design-build research programs and curriculum, with funded research and teaching opportunities for faculty and students.
The department upholds Lehigh University’s Principles of Our Equitable Community, affirming the inherent dignity of every member of our community and working to build a culture of mutual understanding, respect, and academic freedom. We are especially interested in faculty whose research, teaching, design work, and scholarship reflect these principles, whether through studio pedagogy, community engaged practice, or research that examines how the built environment shapes access and opportunity for the communities it serves. These values are central to the department’s mission and purpose.
About Lehigh University
Founded in 1865, Lehigh University has combined outstanding academic and learning opportunities with leadership in fostering innovative research. Recognized among the nation's highly ranked research universities, Lehigh offers a rigorous academic community for over 7,500 students. Lehigh University has some 5,800 undergraduates, 1,800 graduate students, and nearly 600 full-time faculty members. Lehigh University is located in Bethlehem, PA, a vibrant and historic area. Over 840,000 people live in the Lehigh Valley, which is in close proximity to New York City and Philadelphia.
Lehigh University is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital or familial status, national origin (including shared ancestry), pregnancy or related conditions, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or veteran status. Lehigh University is committed to a culturally and intellectually diverse academic community and is especially interested in candidates who can contribute, through their research, teaching and/or service, to this mission. Lehigh University provides competitive salaries and comprehensive benefits, including domestic partner benefits, and supports faculty members’ work/life balance.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Clinical Nursing Part-time - NP-1
jobs.institution: University of Rochester: School of Nursing and Health Sciences
jobs.description:

Candidates must have professional licensure, relevant professional clinical experience, and experience with professional education, education technology, program development, and project management. · Serve as a resource/advisor/mentor for students, including degree planning and academic counseling.
· Support efforts to recruit and retain students by participation in applicant evaluations, attending school events, and ongoing partnership with school personnel in service of our mission.

jobs.institution: The University of Tennessee - Knoxville: Natalie L. Haslam College of Music
jobs.description:
Assistant or Associate Professor; nine-month tenure-track appointment beginning August 1, 2027. Salary and fringe benefits are competitive and commensurate with rank and experience.
The Knoxville campus of the University of Tennessee seeks candidates who have the ability to promote an atmosphere where all members of the university community feel welcome and can thrive.
The responsibilities of this faculty member include teaching bassoon to undergraduate and graduate students through applied lessons and studio classes, as well as teaching the bassoon component of the Double Reed Methods course within the music education curriculum. Haslam College of Music’s chamber music program by developing a sustainable organizational and curricular infrastructure that supports and advances chamber music throughout the College. Responsibilities will include coordinating chamber music activities across areas; working collaboratively with faculty; integrating community outreach and student recruitment initiatives through chamber music; and advancing innovative opportunities for cross-area collaboration, performances, residencies, and related programming.
The successful candidate will be highly organized and collaborative, possess significant experience in chamber music, and demonstrate proficiency and adaptability with administrative processes and technology. They will also bring the vision, initiative, and creativity necessary to develop an innovative, dynamic, and sustainable chamber music program that strengthens artistic collaboration, enriches the student experience, and expands the College’s engagement with its broader community.

jobs.title: Anesthesiologist, Clinical Associate/Full Professor, Anesthesiology, Vice Chair for Clinical Research
jobs.institution: Stony Brook University: Anesthesiology
jobs.description:
Stony Brook Medicine, Department of Anesthesiology has a Vice Chair for Clinical Research faculty position available at the Associate Professor/Professor Level. Tenure vs. non-tenured depending upon experience and qualifications.
Stony Brook University is located 60 miles from New York City on Long Island’s scenic North Shore. Our 1,100-acre campus is home to a diverse community comprised of 25,710 undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students and more than 13,500 faculty and staff, including those employed at Stony Brook Medicine, Suffolk County's only academic medical center and tertiary care provider.
General Responsibilities:
The candidate will provide anesthetic care to patients undergoing surgery or other procedures and will provide consultation before and after the anesthetic procedure. The candidate will be actively engaged in the instruction and/or supervision of medical students, resident physicians and certified registered nurse anesthetists.
Vice Chair for Clinical Research:
Candidate must have a strong track record of peer-reviewed funding in Clinical or translational research, a national/international reputation for research leadership, mentorship, and the ability and desire to develop a strong funded clinical research program. The successful candidate will also have a track record of working with and receiving industry support (pharmaceutical and/or device trials). Duties will include participation and mentorship in departmental activities that pertain to undergraduate, graduate, post-graduate, and faculty research and education. As a member of the executive team, the candidate will be expected to assist in strategic planning and direction, play an important role in administrative aspects pertaining to the initiation of grant support, design of research projects, and organizational aspects related to the research goals of the entire department. The successful candidate will also have the ability and desire to mentor junior clinical faculty to participate and develop their own research projects leading to potential funding, presentations, abstracts and published manuscripts.
We are searching for outstanding candidates with an innovative research program and a history of extramural (Government i.e., NIH, private foundations and industry) pharmaceutical/device manufacturer funding. Candidates must have history of prior or current research and extramural funding. History of publications in high impact journals. Successful candidates are expected to bring their own vigorous dynamic program that would synergize with the ongoing studies at the Department.
The Department and the School of Medicine have excellent research infrastructure, which includes MRI, PET, CT, microscopy, behavioral, genomics and proteomics equipment and facilities.
Existing Research Resources and Support:
The basic and clinical science divisions of the Department have recently undergone major growth and restructuring, with an expanded focus on basic and clinical neuroscience. There are 7 federally funded basic science investigators and some clinical faculty with research and clinical trials experience. Clinical Research Support includes 4 clinical research coordinators and a full-time statistician. Research interests include, but are not limited to, molecular mechanisms of neurodegenerative disorders and chronic pain, adult neurogenesis, learning and memory, brain imaging, mitochondrial dysfunction, ciliopathies, and genomics, investigated on models ranging from Drosophila and frogs to mice and humans.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor Tenure-Track Bioethics and Humanities
jobs.institution: University of Washington: Bioethics & Humanities
jobs.description:
The Department of Bioethics and Humanities at the University of Washington School of Medicine invites applications for a Full-time (100% FTE) faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor Tenure-Track, with an anticipated start date of September 2027. We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment to excellence in research, teaching, and service in a diverse and inclusive academic community.
Assistant Professor Tenure Track appointments hold an initial 3-year renewable term that aligns with a 12-month service period (July 1-June 30). Faculty with 12-month service periods are paid for 11 months of service over a 12-month period (July-June), meaning the equivalent of one month is available for paid time off.
The base salary range for this position will be $6,456 - $10,000 per month, commensurate with experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department of Labor prevailing wage determination.
The successful candidate will be expected to:
Develop a research program of national and international importance in bioethics and humanities. The search’s primary emphasis will be the ethical, social, legal, policy, and/or humanistic dimensions of artificial intelligence (AI) and data-intensive technologies in science, medicine, biomedical research and health care; applications are also welcome from scholars working in other areas of biomedical innovation, including genomics, reproductive and cellular technologies, synthetic biology, and related emerging biotechnologies.
Lead high-quality independent scholarship and publish in peer-reviewed venues.
Pursue extramural research funding, including career-development, investigator-initiated, and/or collaborative awards, as appropriate to support a sustained program of research.
Contribute as a participant in the Department’s Science, Medicine, and Society Lab, a new initiative designed to advance interdisciplinary scholarship, collaborative grant development, teaching, and community-building around social, ethical, historical, legal, policy, and humanistic questions in science, medicine, and society.
Teach and mentor students and trainees across undergraduate, graduate, medical/professional, and other departmental educational programs as appropriate.
Perform service and administrative work that furthers the mission of the department, school, and/or university.
Collaborate effectively across disciplines, cultures, funding sources, and learning environments.
All University of Washington faculty are expected to engage in teaching, research, and service.
About the Department of Bioethics and Humanities
The Department of Bioethics and Humanities is an interdisciplinary department in the University of Washington School of Medicine, with a mission to advance rigorous scholarship, teaching, and public engagement on the ethical, social, historical, and humanistic dimensions of science, medicine, biomedical research and health care. Department faculty work across fields including education, genetics, health services, medical sociology, medicine, philosophy, public health, religious studies and related areas.
Our research and teaching address topics such as, community-based participatory research, clinical and research ethics, biotechnology, social justice and access to health care, global bioethics, medical error, and palliative and end-of-life care.
The Department is deeply connected to the wider UW ecosystem, with collaborative relationships across UW Medicine and the Schools of Law, Nursing, Pharmacy, Public Health, and Social Work, as well as the College of Arts and Sciences and Seattle Children’s. The successful candidate will join a department committed to interdisciplinary scholarship and to building new areas of strength at the intersection of science, medicine and society.
The Department offers an undergraduate minor, a master’s degree in bioethics, professional training programs, and ethics education in the UW School of Medicine.

jobs.title: Lecturer - Computational and Cognitive Neuroscience
jobs.institution: Princeton University: Princeton Neuroscience Institute
jobs.description:
The Princeton Neuroscience Institute seeks a full-time lecturer to teach courses, and /or teach precepts with an anticipated start date of January 16, 2027. The initial appointment will be through July 1, 2027, and may be renewed at 12-month increments, contingent on satisfactory performance and curricular need. The primary responsibility of the successful applicant will be to teach neuroscience laboratory courses for both undergraduate and graduate students in computational and human cognitive neuroscience. The major objective of these courses is to introduce students to both computational modeling as well as the process of experimental design, execution and analysis using modern methods, including large scale electrode recording, fMRI, EEG, fNIRS, MEG, TMS. The successful candidate may have the ability to teach precepts in other departments, as needed. The successful candidate will also have the opportunity to conduct independent research and publish.
The Lecturer will work with faculty to design and update courses where appropriate. They will be responsible for preparing and presenting lectures, laboratory design and setup, creating/ updating assignments utilizing modern open-sourced Python-based analysis tools, writing and grading examinations, meeting with students outside of class time, monitoring teaching assistants, and assigning grades.
Essential Qualifications: Ph.D. in neuroscience or related fields (such as computer science, math or engineering) with a specific focus on relevant applications in computational and human cognitive neuroscience. Proficiency with Python and Jupyter Notebooks. Must have an understanding of mathematical and computational tools used for computational modeling of, and analyzing, behavioral and neuroscientific data. Preferred Qualifications: Experience in teaching at the undergraduate and graduate level. Familiarity with machine learning.
Applicants should submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, teaching statement and contact information for three referees via Interfolio. Preference will be given to candidates who apply by November 30, 2026. This position is subject to the University's background check policy.
We seek faculty members who will create a climate that embraces excellence and diversity, with a strong commitment to teaching and mentoring that will enhance the work of the department and attract and retain a diverse student body, both at the undergraduate and graduate levels.

jobs.title: Open Rank Professor of Management Information Systems
jobs.institution: University of Oklahoma Norman Campus: Division of Management Information Systems
jobs.description:
Open Rank Professor of MIS (Tenured or Tenure-Track)
The University of Oklahoma (OU) invites applications for one open-rank tenured or tenure-track (Assistant, Associate, Full) Professor position in the Management Information Systems (MIS) Division of the Michael F. Price College of Business, beginning in Fall 2027. Our strong programs in the MIS division build on a history of excellence, distinguished faculty, and active industry partnerships. The division offers an undergraduate major and minor in MIS, graduate programs in Business Analytics, both in-person and online, and a Ph.D. degree. It operates the Center for MIS Studies (CMISS), an industry-academic partnership that brings together faculty and business partners to collaborate on research and curriculum development. The division has an active MIS Student Association, provides sizable student scholarships annually, and enjoys strong support from the university and industry partners. The Department of Mathematics at the University of Rochester invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in probability, broadly construed. The University of Rochester is a private, R1 research university located in upstate New York. The mathematics department has a tradition of strength in both research and teaching. Current research areas include mathematical physics, ergodic theory, probability, algebra and number theory, analysis, combinatorics, geometry, and topology. The department has a strong undergraduate program, offering BS and BA degrees in mathematics (both with research honors options), a BS in applied mathematics, and a joint BS degree in mathematics and statistics. There are also certificate programs in operations research and actuarial studies.

Integrate NMR measurements with complementary biophysical and biochemical methods.

Collaborate with researchers within the Fawzi laboratory and across Brown University and external institutions.

The position is particularly well suited for a scientist interested in using NMR not simply as a characterization tool, but as a quantitative approach to understand how biomolecular structure and interactions give rise to biological function, and how these are disrupted in disease.

The Department of Small Animal Clinical Sciences of the University of Tennessee, College of Veterinary Medicine invites applications for a full-time clinical track faculty position in Small Animal Primary Care. The missions of the Department are to educate veterinary students and graduate veterinarians to meet the needs of the pet owning public, to provide advanced patient care, and to generate new knowledge in pet health through basic and applied research. Clinical track faculty at the University of Tennessee are expected to participate in teaching, service, and scholarship programs of the College. Responsibilities of the successful candidate will include clinical service and instruction in small animal primary care to DVM students and house officers, didactic program instruction within the preclinical curriculum, and collaboration in clinical discovery or scholarship.

Specialty services supported by departmental faculty include: internal medicine, oncology, neurology, soft tissue and orthopedic surgery, dentistry, ophthalmology, dermatology, behavior, radiology, radiation oncology, anesthesiology, nutrition, physical therapy, shelter medicine, zoo, and exotic and avian medicine and surgery. Facilities include: nuclear medicine, computerized tomography, MRI, radiation therapy, video endoscopy, laparoscopy, hyperbaric unit, and physical therapy. Pets are seen primarily for wellness, illness, minor surgery, dentistry, and senior screening. The clinic will soon relocate to a newly constructed, full-service primary care clinic separate from the tertiary referral hospital. The successful candidate will join a collaborative service currently staffed by 3 faculty, 2 technicians, and 1 veterinary assistant. Primary care faculty are also committed to developing and supporting spectrum of care opportunities within our college and community.
The University of Tennessee College of Veterinary Medicine boasts a collegial environment committed to mentoring new faculty to be successful in their academic career. The University of Tennessee is located in Knoxville Tennessee, a vibrant small city located between the Great Smoky Mountains and Cumberland plateau, an area with rich biodiversity and natural beauty. The Knoxville Urban Wilderness provides over 50 miles of trails and greenways within the city offering ample opportunity for outdoor recreation. Knoxville has an energetic cultural downtown area with excellent restaurants, bustling farmer’s markets, live music of all genres, ballet, theater, frequent art and cultural festivals, and men’s and women’s sporting events. jobs.title: IFANCA Chair of Indian Muslim Studies and Associate Professor
jobs.institution: Arizona State University: School of Historical, Philosophical and Religious Studies
jobs.description:
About the Position
Arizona State University's The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences invites applications and nominations for the inaugural IFANCA Chair of Indian Muslim Studies, at the rank of Associate Professor, with a start date of August 16, 2027. The Chair will hold tenure in the School of Historical, Philosophical, and Religious Studies (SHPRS) and will be fully embedded in the Center of Muslim Experience in the United States (CME-US), ASU's hub for innovative, publicly engaged scholarship on Muslim life in America and globally.
Position Overview
The inaugural IFANCA (Islamic Food and Nutrition Council of America) Chair of Indian Muslim Studies will be a senior scholar — or a highly accomplished scholar on a strong upward trajectory whose work exemplifies both rigorous humanistic inquiry and the capacity to lead. The Chair will advance innovative research in Indian Muslim Studies, shape CME-US's intellectual agenda, and contribute to ASU's commitments to inclusive excellence, global engagement, and meaningful public scholarship.
About the Center of Muslim Experience in the United States (CME-US)
The Center of Muslim Experience in the United States (CME-US) is a multi-partnership, transdisciplinary research and community outreach center at Arizona State University leading the way in producing transformative scholarship about Muslims in the U.S. that contributes to an American inclusive future.
About the School of Historical, Philosophical, and Religious Studies
ASU’s School of Historical, Philosophical, and Religious Studies (SHPRS) is one of the nation’s largest and most innovative transdisciplinary humanities institutions. With 92 faculty and nearly 1,600 majors, the school teaches more than 33,000 students each year in bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral programs. A substantial portion of the student population is online, including a pioneering master’s program in World War II Studies in collaboration with the National World War II Museum in New Orleans. Additionally, the school hosts transdisciplinary programs and affiliated research and education centers.
About The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences is the academic heart of Arizona State University, committed to improving communities on a local, national and global scale. We support the professional development and growth of our faculty and staff in their cutting-edge research to advance these aims. Within The College, our faculty engage with a large curious student body, guiding them as they grow into socially aware, critical thinkers and writers able to succeed in a wide range of careers and to address the challenges of the twenty-first century. Advancing the success of our students remains our top priority. To learn more about The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, please visit https://thecollege.asu.edu.
About Arizona State University
ASU exemplifies a new prototype for the American public research university. As articulated in the ASU Charter, ASU is a comprehensive public research university, measured not by whom it excludes, but by whom it includes and how they succeed; advancing research and discovery of public value; and assuming fundamental responsibility for the economic, social, cultural and overall health of the communities it serves.
Essential Functions
The successful candidate will be expected to:
The Chair will advance innovative research in Indian Muslim Studies, shape CME-US's intellectual agenda, and contribute to ASU's commitments to inclusive excellence, global engagement, and meaningful public scholarship.
Maintain a distinguished, internationally recognized research and publishing agenda in Indian Muslim Studies within their humanistic discipline
Teach undergraduate and graduate courses aligned with their expertise and in accordance with the curricular needs of the School of Historical, Philosophical, and Religious Studies
Mentor graduate students and junior faculty
Provide intellectual leadership in shaping CME-US's research, programming, and initiatives related to Indian Muslim Studies
Foster interdisciplinary collaboration across ASU, nationally, and internationally
Organize and convene regular conferences, workshops, and seminars
Engage public audiences, community partners, and broader civic life
Supports IFANCA’s mission which includes values of service, adaptability, and integrity and increase awareness through education
Disciplinary Home and Areas of Scholarly Interest
This position is anchored in the Humanities and housed in SHPRS. We particularly welcome scholars working in:
History (including intellectual, social, religious, political, and cultural history)
Religious Studies (anthropology of religion, religious thought, material culture, and contemporary and global religious movements)
Philosophy (including political philosophy, ethics, and philosophy of religion)
Related humanistic fields such as Literary and Cultural Studies, Gender and Justice Studies, Ethnic Studies, Islamic Studies, Asian Studies, or Law and Ethics, where the primary methodology is humanistic
Candidates’ research should focus on Indian Muslim communities in any period (precolonial, colonial, or postcolonial) with attention to contemporary concerns, and may address themes including, but not limited to, pluralism and justice, postcolonial nationalisms, migration and diaspora (with particular attention to Indian Muslims in the United States), law and governance, public narratives and public memory, environmental humanities and ethics, social movements, intellectual history, or everyday lived experience.
Appointment and Support
The IFANCA Endowed Chair comes with a competitive salary, dedicated research funds, and programming support commensurate with rank and experience. The Chair will be fully integrated into CME-US's collaborative environment and is expected to be an active contributor to its mission and community. The position also offers opportunities to collaborate with other ASU centers and initiatives focused on religion and conflict, transborder studies, Asian studies, security studies, and applied ethics.

jobs.description:
The Division of Environment and Sustainability (ENVR) at The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) invites applications and expressions of interest for multiple Research Assistant and Postdoctoral Fellow positions, across three major research areas: Air Quality and Health, Climate Adaptation and Resilience, and Sustainable Economy and Integrated Solutions.
ENVR brings together expertise across environmental science, engineering, health, data science, economics, finance, policy and the social sciences to address complex environmental and sustainability challenges. We are also expanding our capabilities in software development, artificial intelligence and geospatial technologies to support research, education and the translation of research into practical applications.
Air Quality and Health
Our research examines the sources, transport, exposure and health impacts of air pollution, integrating atmospheric observations and modelling with exposure assessment, epidemiology and health-risk analysis. A major objective is to translate scientific understanding into practical information that can better protect public health.
We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise in environmental epidemiology, biostatistics, exposure assessment, air-pollution health research and health-risk modelling. Relevant experience may include time-series or cohort analysis, exposure-response relationships, mortality and morbidity analysis, multi-pollutant and compound environmental risks, and integration of environmental, meteorological, demographic and health datasets.
Experience with R and/or Python, statistical modelling, GIS, data analytics and machine learning would be advantageous.
Climate Adaptation and Resilience
Our research addresses the growing risks associated with climate change and extreme weather, spanning high-resolution weather and climate prediction, climate-risk assessment, early-warning systems, and the “last-mile” challenge of translating warnings into effective actions by individuals and communities.
We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise in one or more of the following areas:
Weather and climate modelling: high-resolution regional and urban weather/climate modelling; model development and process improvement; extreme precipitation, tropical cyclones, heat and other high-impact weather; MPAS or comparable modelling systems; HPC, model evaluation and diagnostics, and analysis of large climate datasets.
Climate risk and early warning: climate-hazard and impact modelling; exposure and vulnerability assessment; impact-based forecasting; development and evaluation of early-warning systems.
Last-mile communication and behavioural response: understanding how people perceive, trust, interpret and respond to climate and extreme-weather warnings, and how warnings can be made more personalized, credible and actionable. Relevant expertise may include social and environmental psychology, behavioural science, risk perception, risk communication, decision-making and behavioural intervention design.
Community engagement and implementation: working with NGOs, community organizations and vulnerable or high-risk population groups to co-design, test and evaluate warning messages, communication channels and practical interventions, including whether warnings reach the intended populations and lead to appropriate protective actions.
Candidates may come from atmospheric science, meteorology, climate science, environmental science, engineering, geography, data science, psychology, behavioural science, public health, social science, risk communication or related disciplines. Interdisciplinary candidates who can connect physical climate-risk information with human behaviour and community implementation are particularly encouraged.
Sustainable Economy and Integrated Solutions
Our research develops practical and integrated approaches to decarbonization, sustainable development and climate resilience, bringing together science and technology with economic, financial and policy considerations.
We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise in one or more of the following areas:
Decarbonization and sustainable transport: maritime and other transport sectors, alternative and low-carbon fuels, lifecycle assessment, carbon accounting, and sustainability and certification of fuel pathways.
Biodiversity and nature-based solutions: ecosystem and biodiversity modelling, spatial analysis, assessment of ecosystem services, and evaluation of nature-based approaches to climate mitigation and adaptation.
Climate risk, economics and finance: quantitative climate-risk assessment, sustainable finance, and the use of insurance and other financial mechanisms to support climate adaptation and resilience.
Relevant backgrounds may include environmental science and engineering, energy and transport, economics and finance, operations research, data science, lifecycle assessment, ecology, environmental management and public policy.
Cross-cutting Software, AI and GIS Development
We are also seeking candidates, particularly at the Research Assistant level, with strong computer science and software-development backgrounds to develop next-generation digital tools supporting environmental research, education and public applications.
We are particularly interested in candidates with experience in one or more of the following:
Web and mobile application development, including interactive spatial web applications, mapping, geospatial analytics, data collection, visualization and field applications;
GIS and geospatial computing, including spatial databases, geoprocessing pipelines, mapping and visualization libraries, and tools such as GDAL/OGR, PostGIS and GeoPandas;
AI-assisted software development and applications, including effective use of large language models, generative AI, APIs and AI coding tools to accelerate development and automate research and data workflows;
Scientific visualization and communication, including interactive visualization, time-series visualization, animation and AI-assisted generation of explanatory and educational materials; and
Development of robust, maintainable scientific software, including appropriate documentation, testing, performance optimization and user-interface design.
Candidates should normally have a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science or a closely related discipline, with sound fundamentals in software engineering, algorithms and data structures. Proficiency in JavaScript/TypeScript, Python and/or mobile development frameworks such as Flutter, React Native, Swift or Kotlin would be valuable.
Experience with web or mobile application development is particularly desirable. Familiarity with geospatial data and environmental applications is advantageous but candidates with a strong computer science background and an interest in applying their skills to environmental and sustainability problems are also encouraged to apply.

The Department of Health Policy & Management at the Bloomberg School of Public Health is seeking an assistant scientist to work with the Major Extremity Trauma Research Consortium (METRC). The position includes a combination of administrative and scholarly activities and requires coordination with investigators and staff from multiple departments and institutions.
The Assistant Scientist will manage and coordinate several multicenter clinical trials supported by METRC. Under the direction of the METRC Coordinating Center Director and Deputy Director Director(s), the Assistant Scientist is responsible for writing narratives for new grant submissions, developing research protocols, managing protocol committees, and overseeing site performance, study enrollment and follow-up, data analysis and communication of results. The role is supported by several grants originating from the Department of Defense and National Institutes of Health, but the research portfolio will change over time, and may include projects funded by private industry or PCORI.

Function independently and serve as a key contributor to study development and design for several multicenter studies.
Collaborate with faculty to develop proposals for funding, focused on the research priorities of METRC.
Lead development of study protocols and data collection forms. Provide oversight and coordination of protocol committee meetings, piloting data collection, and manage research staff within the coordinating center to deliver training on study procedures to research teams at participating clinical centers.
Manage regulatory approvals, amendments, and annual progress reports for each study in accordance with local IRB and sponsor IRB policies.
Design, review, interpret, and integrate data from reports on enrollment, follow-up, and data quality for assigned studies.
Participate in the analysis and interpretation of study results and drafting study reports and papers.

The Department of Biological Sciences at Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) seeks an accomplished scientist and ambitious, collaborative leader to serve as its next head. The head will hold a newly endowed headship in Biological Sciences and will lead the department at a pivotal moment of opportunity, including overseeing the opening of expanded research space and new teaching laboratories in the Richard King Mellon Hall of Science, scheduled to open in early 2028. The candidate will articulate and execute a compelling vision for elevating the department’s scientific impact and external support. The head will advance the quality and visibility of life sciences research across the university, leveraging CMU’s highly collaborative environment and distinctive strengths in computational biology, engineering, computer science, and machine learning to build ambitious interdisciplinary research programs.
The Department of Biological Sciences is one of four departments in the Mellon College of Science. The college also plays a central role in the cross-university Neuroscience Institute, which has strong ties to Biological Sciences. Biological Sciences is home to 20 internationally recognized tenure-track faculty, with strengths in molecular and cellular biology, neuroscience, microbiology, and evolutionary and developmental biology. The tenure-track faculty include a dynamic group of assistant professors hired in the past five years who have already been successful in obtaining external funding. The department has an engaged and collegial community, including 60-70 graduate students, six staff members, postdoctoral fellows, and research scientists. The department also includes 16 teaching-track faculty located in Pittsburgh and at our Qatar campus. Faculty and staff are dedicated to excellence in undergraduate and graduate education, including a PhD program and specialized master’s programs, including Computational Biology and Quantitative Biology and Bioinformatics.
CMU and the department have a long and notable history of innovation and technology development. Faculty in the Department of Biological Sciences have developed new methods for biological imaging, microscopy, molecular visualization, and cell tracking. Currently, faculty in the department hold grants from the NIH, NSF, and multiple private Foundations. The scientific environment in Pittsburgh is vibrant and collaborative. Many faculty hold secondary appointments in other units both within CMU and at the University of Pittsburgh; collaboration through shared graduate students and externally funded research is common.
The successful candidate will have a record of significant scientific achievement and sustained success in securing external research funding. They will bring demonstrated leadership in building research programs, recruiting and developing outstanding faculty, strengthening graduate education, and fostering productive partnerships. They will have a passion for building on the department’s strengths and fostering an environment in which faculty, staff, and students can excel, thereby advancing the department’s ambitions and impact. jobs.description:
The Department of English at Occidental College invites applications for a tenure‐track Open Rank, Professor of British/Anglophone Literature with appointment to begin August 2027.
The English Department is searching for a new colleague in British/Anglophone Literature. The specialization is open, though the department is especially interested in the fields of Long Eighteenth Century, the History of the Novel, Romanticism, British Modernism, Contemporary Global Anglophone literature. We welcome a range of methodologies that practice close reading, examine literary form, and attend to literary history. The new hire will offer courses in Modern British Literature, from its 18th-century origins to its 21st-century manifestations. This will include ENGL 288: Modern British Traditions, as well as other courses at the 100, 200, and 300 levels in their area(s) of specialization. In addition, the new hire will teach required seminar courses that rotate among members of the department, including ENGL 290: Literary Methods, the ENGL 390: Junior Seminar and ENGL 490: Senior Seminar. We are particularly interested in courses that would meet College Core requirements or would engage with the city and communities of Los Angeles. As necessary, the new hire will contribute to the First Year Seminar program, which focuses on writing and community-engagement. The new hire will also have the opportunity to mentor undergraduate researchers in Oxy’s renowned Summer Undergraduate Research Program. The new hire will have an active research agenda, producing scholarship that is commensurate with their rank. Finally, the new hire will participate in the life and development of the department, advise students, and serve on broader college-wide committees.
The Department of English studies literature to develop our critical and creative potential in a nation and world going through drastic changes. We embrace the view that historically, geographically, and culturally grounded readings of literature deepen its aesthetic value. Literature continues to be a wellspring for other creative mediums (including television, film, music, visual art, performance art, and beyond). We also introduce our students to archival research in Occidental’s special collections as well as other libraries and archives in Southern California.
Our students embrace literature’s role in nourishing their critical and creative potential. Every English major researches and writes their own critical analysis of a literary work in their Senior Comprehensive Project. In recent years, students have taken up a range of topics for their Senior Comprehensive, including Gothic fiction,Margaret Atwood’s fiction, Toni Morrison’s fiction, Ecoliterature, Ekphrastic Poetry, Anticolonial Literature, Fantasy Novels, the relationship between Literature and Gaming, and Reginald Shepherd’s Elegies. Our students who take on the creative writing emphasis have completed poetry chapbooks, children’s literature, and short fiction. English majors and minors comprise the majority of the editorial collective that publishes The Oz, Occidental’s literary magazine that features short fiction, poetry, experimental writing, and visual art from students across campus. Our students have also made their mark across Los Angeles, from interning with the Los Angeles Review of Books to volunteering in mutual aid projects. Our graduates go on to work in independent publishing, education, marketing, and law, among other fields. Our faculty are committed teacher-scholars who bring critical inquiry and discovery into the classroom. They establish themselves as exceptional researchers and practitioners in their fields and they provide departmental and college-wide service, as well as service to their professions. As a small institution with a commitment to Shared Governance, faculty across the College collaborate in maintaining the excellence of the College’ academic program.
Located within the vibrant city of Los Angeles, Occidental is committed to a community-engaged curriculum—faculty build fieldwork, visits to local museums and cultural organizations, and long-standing partnerships into their courses. Occidental is also committed to undergraduate research, regularly mentoring students in Occidental’s hallmark summer research program. For decades, Occidental has been a leader in creating access for a diverse student body. That diversity enriches the education of all students. We seek an innovative teacher, scholar, mentor, and colleague who wishes to work in such an environment and who shares the commitments articulated in the mission of the College.

jobs.description:
Georgetown University in Qatar (GU-Q) invites applications for one (1) open-rank core faculty position in International Economics.
We welcome applications from candidates in all fields of economics, with a preference for candidates conducting applied and empirically relevant research. This may include, but is not limited to, fields such as international economics, development economics, behavioral economics, labor economics, political economy, and applied microeconomics and macroeconomics. GU-Q offers a rich academic setting supported by strong institutional resources to enable excellence in teaching and research. Faculty typically teach two courses (or 6 credit hours) per semester (a 2-2 load), supported by best-in-class instructional infrastructure. Access to GU-Q faculty research funds.
Eligibility for funding through the Qatar Research, Development, and Innovation Council (QRDI).
Eligibility to apply for a summer research supplement equivalent to 2/9 of base salary.
Generous conference travel funding and professional development resources.

GU-Q offers a highly competitive compensation package by U.S. academic standards, along with an exceptional expatriate benefits package that includes:
Fully furnished, high-quality housing.
Transportation allowance.
Annual family home leave.
Worldwide health insurance coverage.
Private school tuition support for accompanying children.
Additional relocation and onboarding assistance.

GU-Q was established in 2005 alongside other elite international universities in Education City, in partnership with Qatar Foundation. For more information on GU-Q, see https://www.qatar.georgetown.edu.

Public parks, beaches, sports facilities (including Education City’s extensive sports venues), museums, cafes, and restaurants abound, and a state-of-the-art metro system connects all parts of Doha and nearby locations. Within Education City, the iconic Qatar National Library, designed by Rem Koolhaas, provides free membership to faculty and students. Faculty at GU-Q also benefit from a close-knit Georgetown community, strong institutional support, and regular coordination between Doha and Washington, D.C. While the early months of 2026 brought instability to the region, Doha remains one of the safest cities in the world, and Qatar continues to rank highly in the Global Peace Index. Doha is connected by direct flights to more than 160 destinations in 90 countries. This short video offers a glimpse of what it is like to teach and live in Qatar.

The Department of Molecular Biosciences at the University of Texas at Austin invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant Professor level in the field of biochemistry, with an emphasis on metabolism. We are particularly interested in collaborative and interdisciplinary scientists passionate about pursuing a mechanistic understanding of intermediary metabolism and metabolic regulation, elucidating connections with core biological processes or metabolic dysfunction, and developing innovative approaches to study cell metabolism. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, cellular and organellar metabolism, metabolic signaling, systems and computational approaches to metabolism, enzymology and metabolic regulation, structural and chemical biology of metabolic pathways, and the biochemical underpinnings of metabolic diseases (e.g., diabetes, obesity, tumor metabolism, and inborn errors of metabolism).
The Department of Molecular Biosciences is composed of a broad faculty whose research interests span many disciplines including biochemistry, molecular biology, structural biology and biophysics, cell and developmental biology, plant biology, microbiology, immunology and infectious diseases, biotechnology, and systems and synthetic biology. We are excited to welcome collaborative scientists who actively interact with our faculty members and take advantage of our state-of-the-art facilities (see below).
Successful candidates are expected to establish and sustain a vibrant research program; serve as dedicated teachers and mentors at both the undergraduate and graduate levels; and assist in the administrative and governance functions of the department, the university, and the profession via service on committees as appropriate. Applicants at the assistant professor level must have plans to develop an exciting independent research program and a strong commitment to graduate and undergraduate education.
“What starts here changes the world.” UT Austin offers numerous resources and an exciting and interactive environment to foster creative interdisciplinary research. In addition to their research activities, our faculty are committed to the development of state-of-the art courses and real-world training experiences for undergraduate and graduate students as part of our core educational mission. Successful candidates will be eligible for membership in the Interdisciplinary Life Sciences Graduate Programs, which includes the Biochemistry Graduate Program, and collectively recruit a talented pool of graduate students each year. We also have outstanding core facilities, including those within the Center for Biomedical Research Support, the Texas Advanced Computing Center, and the Sauer Center for Structural Biology. The department has strong ties to other research units at UT Austin, including the School of Engineering, School of Pharmacy, Department of Computer Science, Oden Institute for Computational Engineering & Sciences, and Dell Medical School. This position offers excellent start-up funds, salary, and laboratory space in a dynamic and highly interactive research environment in the vibrant city of Austin.
